channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Britain Will ‘Heed Warnings’ Over AI, Burnham’s Deputy Says
item.description: The UK government said it will work with other countries on the safety of artificial intelligence after warnings that the technology must be slowed to prevent it from inflicting catastrophic harm.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham

item.title: France Lobbies EU to Lift Sanctions on Russian Tycoon Usmanov
item.description: France is pushing European Union member states to lift sanctions on Russian billionaire Alisher Usmanov as part of a prisoner release deal with Azerbaijan, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Nardelli

item.title: Trump’s Defense of AI Adds to Midterms Risk
item.description: US President Donald Trump’s opposition to guardrails on artificial intelligence puts him at odds with a growing number of lawmakers from both parties, with AI safety fears adding to voters’ misgivings about the technology heading into the midterm elections. Bloomberg's Anthony Stephens breaks down the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: What’s at Stake for Putin in Russia’s Duma Election?
item.description: Russians are set to go to the polls to elect a new lower house of parliament for the first time since President Vladimir Putin ordered the 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Burnham Weighs Offering Saudi Arabia Support
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham is considering whether to help Saudi Arabia counter attacks from the Houthis in Yemen as UK concerns about a worsening economic hit from the escalating conflict grow. The Saudi government has requested a range of diplomatic and military support from the UK, but it's unclear whether Burnham is willing to approve them. Bloomberg's Stuart Livingstone-Wallace has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: NATO Shoots Down Drone That Entered Lithuanian Airspace
item.description: NATO jets shot down an unidentified drone that flew into the Lithuanian airspace from neighboring Belarus early Tuesday, the latest incursion on the alliance’s eastern flank as aerial warfare between Ukraine and Russia intensifies.
item.dc:creator: Milda Seputyte

item.title: Japan Eyes Defense Spending at 3.5% of GDP After US Pressure
item.description: Japan is considering a new mid-term defense spending target of 3.5% of GDP in line with NATO and other US allies, a move that could send a shockwave through financial markets concerned about Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s spending plans.
item.dc:creator: Alastair Gale

item.title: US Backs New Pacific Cable as China Rivalry Reshapes Networks
item.description: The US Trade and Development Agency on Monday announced funding for a feasibility study on a new trans-Pacific submarine cable linking the US with Thailand and as many as five other Southeast Asian nations, as Washington seeks to expand secure digital infrastructure in the region.
item.dc:creator: Philip J. Heijmans

item.title: Denmark Says Russian Warship Fired Flares at Helicopter
item.description: Denmark’s military said a warship from Russia fired flares toward a Danish helicopter, the latest sign of worsening tensions between the two countries.
item.dc:creator: Christian Wienberg and Sanne Wass

item.title: Hegseth, Pistorius Eye Deal For EU Firms to License US Weapons
item.description: German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius will discuss closer defense-industry cooperation in talks with his US counterpart Pete Hegseth in Washington on Tuesday as Europe looks to fill its low stocks of air defense missiles and deep-strike weapons.
item.dc:creator: Michael Nienaber

item.title: Pentagon Sees Strategic Inventory Munitions Shortfalls, IG Says
item.description: The US fired so many munitions at Iranian targets during the first few months of Operation Epic Fury that it “has resulted in strategic inventory shortfalls and revealed industrial base bottlenecks for munitions resupply,” Pentagon officials acknowledged to the Defense Department’s independent watchdog.
item.dc:creator: Tony Capaccio

item.title: Singapore Reviewing Report on Officials’ Home-Buying Patterns
item.description: Singapore said it’s reviewing a research paper that alleged the city-state’s civil servants disproportionately bought homes near planned subway stations that weren’t yet publicly announced to generate “meaningful private gains.”
item.dc:creator: Gabrielle Ng

item.title: Obama Calls For AI Safety Measures, Rebuking Trump Approach
item.description: Former President Barack Obama voiced support for federal laws and regulations governing artificial intelligence safety, saying that the technology could unleash “potential catastrophe” if not properly managed.
item.dc:creator: Jordan Fabian

item.title: Supreme Court Rejects Trump’s Mail Ballot Curbs for Midterms
item.description: The US Supreme Court refused to clear the Postal Service to enforce new restrictions on mail-in ballots for the congressional midterm elections, rebuffing the Trump administration’s request to intervene after several states launched early voting.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Tillman

item.title: Trump: AI ‘Taking Over the World...is a Hoax'
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Douglas Holtz-Eakin, President of the American Action Forum and former Director of the Congressional Budget Office, says the Federal Reserve should raise interest rates this week and warns that failing to do so would undercut its credibility as inflation remains its central challenge. David Sacks, chair of the President's Council of Advisors on Science & Technology, says Anthropic and OpenAI should slow development of their most advanced AI models if they believe the technology poses serious risks, but argues they don’t need new regulation to do it. Steven Cook, senior fellow for Middle East and Africa studies at the Council on Foreign Relations, says Saudi Arabia made a “grave miscalculation” in confronting the Houthis and now finds itself in an “extraordinarily strategically vulnerable position.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Venezuela’s Acting Leader Rodríguez Is Said to Plan UN Visit
item.description: Venezuela’s acting President Delcy Rodríguez is planning to attend the United Nations General Assembly in New York next week, a visit that would mark a major step in the rapid normalization of relations between Caracas and the Trump administration, according to people familiar with the plans.
item.dc:creator: Andreina Itriago and Eric Martin

item.title: Colombian Lawmakers Pass 16% Budget Rise That Worried Investors
item.description: Colombian lawmakers greenlit a 16% increase in government spending for next year, a budget that alarmed investors already nervous about the nation’s growing debt burden.
item.dc:creator: Oscar Medina

item.title: Trump Energy Boss Says Fuel Export Ban Wouldn’t Cut Fuel Prices
item.description: One of President Donald Trump’s top energy chiefs said a US ban on fuel exports or crude wouldn’t bring down pump prices.
item.dc:creator: Ari Natter

item.title: UK Mulls Supporting Saudis Amid Fears of Houthi Economic Hit
item.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is considering whether to help Saudi Arabia counter attacks from the Houthis in Yemen amid British concerns about a worsening economic hit from the escalating conflict.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham

item.title: Germany, UniCredit Say Commerzbank Talks Were ‘Constructive’
item.description: German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil and UniCredit SpA Chief Executive Officer Andrea Orcel said they held constructive talks Monday after the ministry outlined the demands it has for the Italian lender’s bid to take over Commerzbank AG.
item.dc:creator: Arno Schütze, Sonia Sirletti and Kamil Kowalcze
